title: Start here: what Summit Ready is, and how this guide works
kind: the chapter to read before you open Visual Studio 2019
one: You meet Summit Ready, the game this guide builds, and the topics your own game may not use. You find out how the code blocks, the Your turn screens and the ticks in this guide work.

stages.title: Meet Summit Ready, the game this guide builds

screens.title: See every window of Summit Ready, from logging in to saving a score

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know every window of Summit Ready, in the order a player meets them.
Summit Ready is a game made in Visual Studio 2019 with C#. This guide shows you how to build it, one chapter at a time. As you build each part, you make it your own.

words: A small window with a message and an OK button. `MessageBox.Show` opens one.
One window of your game. Summit Ready has a form for logging in, a form for the map, and a form for each game.

blocks.intro: You do not need to learn these words now. Where you first meet each one in the chapter, it has a dotted line under it. Hover over it or tap it to see what it means.

blocks.p: Summit Ready is for pupils going on their first hill-walking expedition. It makes them practise the skills they find tricky: what to pack, reading the weather, grid references, timing a route and knots.
Each window of the game is called a [[form|1]]. A player meets the forms in the order on this screen.
The first form is Log in. A player types a username and a password, then clicks **Log in**. After 3 wrong tries in a row, the form makes the player wait 30 seconds.

screenshot.alt: The Summit Ready Log in form, with a photo of the Mourne Mountains, a Username box, a Password box and a gold Log in button.
screenshot.cap: The Log in form. A new player clicks **Register a new player** under the Log in button.

blocks.p: A new player signs up on the Register form. The player picks a username, types a password twice, and clicks a picture.
The picture is the player's avatar. An avatar is the small picture that stands for the player in the game.

screenshot.alt: The Register a new player form, with 3 boxes on the left and 8 animal pictures on the right.
screenshot.cap: The Register form. The 8 avatars are a goat, an eagle, a fox, a hare, a deer, an owl, a badger and a raven.

blocks.p: After logging in, the player sees the Welcome form. It shows the player's avatar, their best score, and the Top 10 climbers.

screenshot.alt: The Welcome form, with a fox avatar on the left and a Top 10 climbers table on the right.
screenshot.cap: The Welcome form. The **Start the expedition** button opens the map.

blocks.p: The map shows 8 real summits in the Mourne Mountains. Each summit is one game, and the player can climb them in any order.

screenshot.alt: The Your expedition map, with 8 red flags on the left and a list of the 8 summits on the right.
screenshot.cap: The map. Each summit in the list on the right opens its game.

blocks.p: When the player clicks **Finish the expedition**, the Feedback form shows the score for each game. It says what went well and what went wrong, in full sentences.

screenshot.alt: The Feedback form. The player scored 83 out of 800 points, and Pack the Rucksack is picked in the list.
screenshot.cap: The Feedback form after one game. Clicking **Save my score** saves the score and goes back to the Welcome form.

screens.title: See the 8 games, and choose any 4 of them

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know the 8 games in Summit Ready, and how many of them you build.
Each game is played in a different way, so each game teaches you a different piece of C#.
Chapters 11 to 18 each build one game. You build any 4 of the 8 games. You may build more than 4 if you have time.

screenshot.alt: Pack the Rucksack after Check my rucksack. Each item has a tick or a cross, and the bottom line says 10 of 12 in the right place.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 11, Pack the Rucksack: drag each item to **Pack it** or **Leave it at home**.

screenshot.alt: Knot Pairs at the start of a round, with 16 cards face down and Tries: 0 of 24.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 12, Knot Pairs: turn over two cards at a time to match each knot to its name.

screenshot.alt: Leave No Trace before the walk starts, with a fox avatar on a field of grass, 8 pieces of litter and 3 sheep.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 13, Leave No Trace: walk with the arrow keys, pick up the litter, and keep away from the sheep.

screenshot.alt: Read the Sky on question 1 of 10, with a photo of a ring of light round the sun and 3 answer buttons.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 14, Read the Sky: pick the best answer before the time bar runs out.

screenshot.alt: Whiteout during a round, with the hidden word, the letter buttons and the cloud coming down over the picture.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 15, Whiteout: guess the hidden word one letter at a time, before the cloud comes all the way down.

screenshot.alt: Grid Ref Rescue on rescue 1 of 5, with a map with numbered grid lines and a radio message.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 16, Grid Ref Rescue: click the grid square that the radio message gives you.

screenshot.alt: Route Timer on leg 1 of 5, with a photo of a hill, a slider and the line Your guess: 1 hour 10 minutes.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 17, Route Timer: slide to your guess of how long a walk takes, then lock it in.

screenshot.alt: Listen Out on sound 1 of 10, with a gold Play the sound button and 4 pictures.
screenshot.cap: Chapter 18, Listen Out: play the sound, then click the picture that made it.

blocks.p: In Summit Ready, each game scores up to 100 points, so a perfect expedition scores 800 points. In your own game, you choose how many points each question is worth.
You pick your 4 games in chapter 1. Chapters 2 to 10 come before the games, because every game needs them.

stages.title: Choose a topic that Summit Ready does not use

screens.title: Keep your own game away from the Summit Ready topics

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know which topics your own game may not use.
Your game must be your own work. So your game may not use the topic of Summit Ready, or any topic close to it.

Your game may not be about mountains, hill-walking, expeditions or the Duke of Edinburgh's Award. It may not be about camping, outdoor pursuits, map reading or navigation, knots, or weather forecasting.
The pictures, questions and words in Summit Ready may not appear in your finished game either.
A good [[topic|2]] is something that people find tricky, or want to practise. It can be a school subject, such as French verbs, key dates in history, or the parts of a plant cell.
It can also be something outside school, such as the steps taught at a local dance class, or the rules of a sport you play.
In chapter 1, you choose your topic, who your game is for, and your 4 games.

stages.title: Learn how the code blocks, the Your turn screens and the ticks work

screens.title: Read the four kinds of code block

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know what to do with each kind of code block in this guide.
Every code block has a label in its top left corner. The label tells you what to do with the code.
A block labelled **Type this one** has yellow lines. You type the yellow lines yourself, because typing new code is how you learn it.
You do not type anything now. The block below is only to show you what a **Type this one** block looks like.

code.title: An example of a block you type
partLines: This line shows a small window with the words **Player created** and an OK button.

blocks.p: Click **Walk me through it** under any block to see what each part of the code does, one part at a time.
A block labelled **Copy this one** has a **Copy it** button. You copy code that you have already typed somewhere earlier in the guide.
Some blocks give you the code with a gap. You copy the block, then type the missing part yourself, where it says `// YOU TYPE THIS PART`.
A block labelled **Read this one** is there to read. It shows code or a data file that you need to understand, but do not type.

code.title: An example of a block you read: one line of players.txt
partLines: This line is one player. The bar `|` splits it into 4 parts: the username, the password, the avatar picture and the date the player joined.

blocks.p: A block labelled **Your turn** is a task you do on your own. Try it yourself first.
If you are stuck, click **Stuck? Show me the finished code** under the task to see an answer.
Your teacher can see which blocks you copied and which answers you opened. That is normal and it is not a punishment. It shows your teacher where the guide needs to help more.
Each new piece of C# follows the same order. The first time you meet it, you type it. The second time, you copy it with a gap. After that, you copy it.

screens.title: Make each part your own as you build it

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how your game turns from Summit Ready into your own game, one part at a time.
You do not build all of Summit Ready first and change it at the end. Each chapter builds one part, tests it, then has a **Your turn** screen to [[make it yours|3]].
For example, chapter 5 builds the Register window. Its **Your turn** screen swaps the animal avatars for your own pictures.
Once you change a part, your screen shows your own words, pictures and numbers. Later steps still show Summit Ready's. That is how it should be, so carry on.
If a later test names a Summit Ready word that you changed, look for your own word in its place.
Change anything else you like too, as long as the tests still pass.

screens.title: Tick each step and test as you finish it

blocks.p: By the end of this screen, you will know how to tick your work, and where to find your place next time.
Each step in the guide has a numbered tick button on its left. Click the tick button when you have done the step.
Each test in a test table has a tick button too. Tick a test when it has passed.
Your ticks save, because you signed in. The next time you open a chapter, its button says **Carry on**, and the top of the chapter shows how many steps are ticked.
There is no printed copy of this guide. You always use it signed in, so your ticks and your place are saved.
When you finish a chapter, click **Mark chapter 0 as done** at the bottom of its last screen. If you want to start a chapter again, click **Clear my ticks**.
Some words have a dotted line under them. Hover over the word, or tap it, to see what it means.
Under many steps there is a line that starts **If it goes wrong**. Click it if your screen does not match the step.
Run each check below before you go on to chapter 1. Tick each check when it is true for you.

check.what: You have a first idea for a topic, and for who will play your game.
check.how: Say your idea in one sentence, such as a game about French verbs for KS3 pupils.

check.what: Your first idea for a topic is NOT on the list of Summit Ready topics.
check.how: If your game is about camping, knots or the weather, it is too close to Summit Ready. Pick another topic.
check.fix: Read the list of topics again on the screen called **Keep your own game away from the Summit Ready topics**.

check.what: You know that each chapter ends by making the part it built your own.
check.how: Each chapter from chapter 2 has a **Your turn** screen for your own words, pictures or numbers.
